title: Restore and validate disaster-recovered services
question: In what dependency order can the service be restored, and which technical, security, and business gates must pass before traffic resumes?
scenario: A portal is restored from a clean image, but the identity provider uses a changed signing key and the monitoring agent is not enrolled in the recovery environment.
focalRelation: in this payment-service scenario, facility/network/DNS/time are declared dependencies of identity and key services in this payment-service scenario, identity/key services are declared dependencies of data and application restoration component availability --technical gate only--> candidate service security control and integrity checks --security gate--> protected candidate business transaction and owner sign-off --business gate--> resume traffic return to normal --separate controlled change--> closure

states.title: Case facts fixed
states.caption: A portal is restored from a clean image, but the identity provider uses a changed signing key and the monitoring agent is not enrolled in the recovery environment.

states.title: Controlling condition identified
states.caption: Assessment updates the recovery decision when the event changes the assumptions.

states.title: Tempting shortcut rejected
states.caption: If the application responds, restoration is complete. Identity, data integrity, keys, authorization, monitoring, dependencies, performance, and business workflow still require validation.

states.title: Bounded action applied
states.caption: Keep the portal in controlled recovery status. Re-establish key and identity trust, validate authorization and session behavior, enroll monitoring, test customer workflows and data integrity, and obtain business and security acceptance before opening traffic. Record the dependency gap and update the DR build sequence.

states.title: Outcome accepted with limits
states.caption: Given an activated DR event, sequence restoration, validate integrity and security, obtain service acceptance, and document residual risk and lessons. The case record retains the scope, owner, exceptions, and evidence used for this conclusion.

states.title: Decision recomputed
states.caption: Keep the service constrained, correct and test authorization and monitoring, obtain acceptance, and document the RTO result and security delay separately. A fast but unauthorized or unobservable service is not a safe recovery.

states.title: Changed outcome verified
states.caption: The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

options.feedback: Incorrect: Identity, data integrity, keys, authorization, monitoring, dependencies, performance, and business workflow still require validation.

options.label: Keep the portal in controlled recovery status

retry.prompt: Restored data matches its checksum, but inherited access roles include departed administrators. Should the service be accepted?

options.label: Constrain service, remove stale roles, test controls, and obtain accountable acceptance
options.feedback: Correct. Data integrity does not prove current identity and authorization state.

options.label: Accept it because matching checksums prove the restored service is trustworthy
options.feedback: Checksums support data integrity only; stale privileged roles remain a security failure.

options.label: Discard the restored data and repeat recovery even though the data is intact
options.feedback: The stated defect is authorization state; correct and validate it rather than destroying valid restored data.

retry.hint: One successful validation dimension does not satisfy the others.

takeaway: Keep the portal in controlled recovery status.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implemented in 5 stable state states: Restored portal image enters security validation as candidate only Security validation; Changed identity signing key blocks trusted token and session checks until repaired Security validation. The model keeps Restored portal image, Changed identity signing key, Missing monitoring enrollment, Security validation, Business workflow test, Traffic acceptance distinct. Its changed case is “The alternate service meets its RTO, but validation finds stale authorization roles and no alert when a recovery administrator changes them.” and every option returns to a named repair state.

learningJob.plainExplanation: An application response is not proof of complete restoration. Identity, keys, data integrity, authorization, monitoring, performance, dependencies, business workflow, and residual risk require validation and acceptance.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: The dependency chain with separate technical, security, and business gates shows exactly why application response precedes rather than equals accepted recovery.
